top.line: A Kickstarter plan: a sovereign website on a Raspberry Pi or a tablet, five tiers, local AI on the Pro ones.

in-short.line: An appliance on Kickstarter, five tiers, local AI on the Pro tiers, the Pi cheaper at each level, the UK first.

product.line: A tablet or a Raspberry Pi with the site, editing and monitoring; on the Pro tiers, a local AI model too.

android.line: Android is open and fully ours; the Web Summit tablet is the prototype; iOS a stretch goal.

tiers.line: £50 supporter; £400 Pi; £500 tablet; £900 Pi Pro; £1,000 tablet Pro; add-ons for an app or a product.
tiers.para: The Pi is cheaper at each level.

hardware.line: iRasptek Pi 5 kits £229.99 (8GB) and £397.99 (16GB), Lenovo Idea Tab £209.99, Galaxy Tab S10 FE £509, Volla.

on-device.line: The Pro tiers run a local model and can build a website on the device; the standard ones run a site we build.

pi.line: The Pi as one host alongside GitHub Pages, reached without proprietary tunnels where possible.

goals.line: The UK as the base goal, Portugal first, then countries by vote, and iOS; appliances launch after the campaign.

value.line: Every backer sees their own site in a vault before anything ships.

partners.line: Launch with Android and open source, then talk to device makers as a funded project.

after.line: Late pledges, pre-orders on sovereignwebsite.ai, and Patreon later.

limits.line: Nothing submitted; prices are examples; local AI on the Pro devices to be tested; device software a plan; no goal yet.

sources.line: The afternoon's record, UK retailers' pages and Amazon UK Pi kit listings on 19 November.
